reason: The repo is a blockchain node and network runtime (VOID Chain, Buy VOID, DataNet) whose purpose isn't producing software with agents, and agent-driven commits and PRs build it.
It's a desktop app that orchestrates teams of AI coding agents (kanban, task assignment, agent review), and it has AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md and agent-driven commit cadence.
AgentMux is an environment for running and coordinating fleets of coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, swarm, inter-agent messaging), and its own commits come from named agents via a bot.

The README describes a personal infrastructure monorepo (Bazel, Nix, cluster, many unrelated apps), and agents land PRs in it. It is not itself a coding-agent orchestrator, though agentplane is a sub-project.
It's a sandbox (microVM) wrapper for running coding agents securely, not an orchestrator that produces code; commits are by Claude agents (claude/ branches, Co-Authored-By Claude).
It is a database of AI model specs stored as TOML files, and the recent commits are all bot "chore(sync): update ... model catalog" data refreshes, not code changes.

The README describes an "AI game engine and agent orchestration framework" (kernel, memory, swarm, API, installer), a runtime product. The Builder Plane is a secondary part, and the commits are agent-written masterplan and layer modules.

It's a quantitative finance research harness and fx-1 training pipeline (src/fx1, quant_fund). Agent identities like "Coder" and kimi-lane sweeps commit to it, but it doesn't orchestrate coding agents.
ADE is a workspace for running and managing fleets of coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, worktree lanes, automations, Linear agent), and its commits are co-authored by Claude agents.
Described as an "autonomous software factory" that turns issues into verified PRs with AI agents, and its commits show agent slices, TL review rounds and Claude-Session trailers.

Its Chief of Staff orchestrates fleets of coding agents (Claude Code, Codex) that write and land code, and PortOS develops itself via agent "claim/issue-N" PRs; it is also a broad personal app, hence medium.
Genie is a CLI that dispatches parallel coding agents in worktrees to produce reviewed PRs, and the README says it is built with Genie itself.
It is a command center and fleet manager for running Claude Code, Codex and other coding agents across machines, and commits show Claude co-authorship with about 35 merged PRs a day.
Atomic is a coding agent runtime for orchestrating staged, verifiable agent workflows ("software factories"), and its commits carry Assistant-model trailers showing agents develop it.
Beadhive is described as an automated "software factory" CLI that orchestrates agent seats and beads work (merge, molecule, worktrees, validation lanes), and its own commits are bead-driven merges.
The repo is an ICT crypto/futures trading bot (Bybit, IBKR, strategies) that Claude sessions build and merge through PRs. It is a trading app, not a tool for orchestrating coding agents.

Commits are all from agent identities (e.g. arm-005__claude-fable-5-1__grasp-cube) mirroring agent-written Python robot-arm tools; the agents grasp cubes rather than build software, so this isn't an orchestrator.
Agent-Native is a framework for building agentic apps (Clips, Design, Slides, Analytics), not a tool that orchestrates agents writing code, and it has heavy agent-driven commits and PRs.
The repo is a from-scratch C compiler and toolchain monorepo, and Claude and Codex agents land its PRs. It is not a tool for orchestrating coding agents.
It's a platform for persistent, continually learning AI personas, not mainly a coding-agent pipeline. Commits show agents like Kimi and Claude landing its Rust code through cards and reviews.
Monorepo of Next.js affiliate pet-site code (domains, shop buttons, Amazon Associates), with Cursor Agent co-authored PRs; it builds websites rather than orchestrating coding agents.
Carrick is a Rust hybrid Linux kernel/runtime, not an agent orchestrator. AGENTS.md, handoff files and "director"/review-style commits show agents building it.

Commits are Codex agents reviewing and checkpointing mathematics roadmaps, sources and Lean signatures, so the content is formal math and roadmaps, even though a small atlas viewer app sits alongside it.
The repo is an Agda formal-proof workspace (theorems on Moonshine, P!=NP, Hodge, YM), so it is mainly formal mathematics, not an agent-orchestration tool or an application.

README describes an infrastructure platform (Backstage, Flux, LiteLLM) hosting other products, built by estate-agents bot commits; the `factory/` and `.crew.json` entries hint at agent orchestration but aren't the purpose.
Xum is a desktop "coding agent multiplexer" that runs isolated parallel agent workspaces (with its own agent loop), and its own 🤖-tagged PRs land at about 34 per day.
Remudero is an orchestration harness that runs Claude Code and Codex workers through a plan→implement→review→merge loop, and its own PRs are landed by that fleet (bot commits, self-hosting).
diri is a native app for running and orchestrating fleets of parallel coding agents (MCP spawning, worktrees, review), and its commits are co-authored by Claude Opus.
re-frame2 is a ClojureScript front-end framework with spec, devtools and HTTP effects; commits cite beads and AGENTS.md/.claude, so agents build it, but it doesn't orchestrate agents.
It's a Next.js interactive Einstein critical-edition site with physics labs, built by agents (AGENTS.md, beads task graph, ~237 commits/day), not a tool for orchestrating coding agents.
It is a Rust JS/TS runtime (parser, Intl, module fixes with bd- bead IDs, AGENTS.md, .agent-mail), not a tool that orchestrates coding agents.
NTM spawns and coordinates fleets of AI coding agents (Claude, Codex) in tmux with work assignment and file reservations, and its commits are co-authored by Claude.

It's a paper-trading research and backtesting platform (strategies, risk, execution, validation) with AGENTS.md and heavy bot commits, so the product is trading software, not an agent-orchestration tool.
It's a videogame (a witch rave in a forest, Three.js/TypeScript), and Claude-authored commits and PRs build it. It isn't a tool for orchestrating agents.
ripr is a Rust static-analysis CLI/LSP tool for test-gap evidence, not an agent orchestrator, and its commits (Claude co-authors, ~40 merged PRs a day) show agents building it.
Everruns is a Rust agent framework/runtime platform for running agents, not a tool that orchestrates agents writing code, and it is developed with agents (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, high PR volume).
The repo is a Rust B-rep CAD kernel with a GUI and Python bindings, and Claude-authored commits and orchestrator trackers show agents building it. The product is not an agent orchestrator.
The repo is a chess game and studio (War Room, Chronicles RPG, Football, Home scene). It has a React frontend and Go/Python backends, and it is not a tool for orchestrating coding agents.

Flapjack is a Lean port of the Pancake verified compiler, which is a software project. Agents build it: commits are co-authored by Claude, and the branches are named for a fleet. It doesn't orchestrate coding agents itself.
Arrowz is a puzzle generator, CLI, web component and lab, with AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md and agent-driven PR flow. It is a software product, not a tool for orchestrating coding agents.
It's a Rust trading-connectivity library (venue crates, order management, codecs) whose commits are Claude-co-authored and reviewed by agents; it isn't a tool for orchestrating coding agents.
Jazz is a local-first relational database (Rust/TS) with AGENTS.md and claude/-named branches, so agents build it, but it isn't an agent orchestrator.
Gas City is an orchestration SDK for multi-agent coding workflows (controller, sessions, formulas, beads work routing), and its heavy agent-driven commit activity shows it is developed by agents.
Paseo is an agentic development environment that orchestrates parallel coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, etc.) in worktrees, and its commits come from bots and AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md-driven agents.
gh-aw compiles agent workflows (Copilot, Claude, Codex) that open PRs via safe-outputs, and its own commits are mostly agent-authored PRs (Copilot, Co-authored-by trailers).

Scion is an orchestration platform for running teams of AI coding agents (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex) in containers, and it has agent-oriented files (AGENTS.md, .scion, .tasks) and a very high-volume PR cadence.
agent-afk is a coding agent harness with orchestrators (/mint, /ship, daemon) that build and verify features autonomously, and its own PRs are agent-driven (issue-numbered fixes, bot releases).
It's the Daglang compiler (Rust, "Home of the Daglang compiler"). A bot with Claude co-author trailers lands nearly all commits. It's a compiler, not an agent orchestrator.
It's a decompilation and native Linux/Vulkan runtime for NFS SHIFT, with agent-style commits (analyzer, evidence, test, docs) and lane-based processes; it builds a game, not an agent orchestrator.
HOL Guard is a runtime security tool (Python/Rust) that guards agents rather than orchestrating them to write code; its commits and merged PRs come around the clock from agent-driven development.
A matching decompilation of Total Annihilation (C++ source, AGENTS.md, Claude-assisted commits) is a software project built by agents, not a tool for orchestrating agents.
HyperFrames is a video-rendering framework (HTML to MP4 via CLI, engine, studio). Its skills help agents use it but don't orchestrate agents that land code, and agents appear to build it.
Fern is a programming language and compiler (Go oracle plus a self-hosted compiler), not an agent orchestrator; the codex/ PR branches and ~228 commits a day show agents building it.
MASC assembles Keeper agents that divide tasks, verify and land work via a Board and MCP, and it is itself developed by Claude-co-authored agent commits and bot merges.

Soleur is a Claude Code/Codex/Devin plugin with 67 agents, 103 skills and a plan/review/ship workflow that orchestrates agents to land code, and its own PRs are agent-written (plan, review, Claude co-author trailers).
ArchLucid is a C# architecture-analysis product (API, CLI, application projects) whose commits are co-authored by Cursor agents, so it's an app built by agents, not an agent orchestrator.
Kosmos is an agent management platform that creates and supervises Claude agents, and its commits are agent-written (Claude co-authored, "challenge-loop", "board review" iterations).

The README describes Jovie as a Next.js artist-profile/link-in-bio product, built by agents. Many commits tune its fleet-gate and merge-queue tooling, but that supports the app rather than being the product.
The repo is a Three.js management-sim game, and its README says a team of Claude Code agents built it. The product is a game, not agent tooling.

AutoMobile is an MCP server and libraries for mobile automation and testing (a product, not an agent-orchestrated code factory), and agents are building it, given about 94 merged PRs per day and AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md.
It's a desktop kanban board that spawns and orchestrates coding-agent CLIs in worktrees, and its commits carry Claude Co-Authored-By trailers and agent review passes.
It's a Texas lifestyle publication site (TypeScript app with Supabase and Cloudflare deploy) built by agents (AGENTS.md, ~50 merged PRs a day), not a tool for orchestrating agents.
Kody is a Cloudflare Workers/MCP personal-assistant app (multi-user SaaS with billing and orgs) whose commits come from Devin and Cursor bots, but it is not itself an agent orchestrator.

The README calls it "a research dataset with renderers attached," and the commits are ticket work on historical cards, households, sources and rulings; the viewer code is secondary to that research content.
Recent commits are about generated video shots (Kling renders, "B56 v4", "SC05-T6 v17", Act 6 fixes) for products like stryde-71-stairs-man, so the repo is mostly media content, not code.
Gnoblin is a Mutter-based compositor/session runtime (C, Lua), not an agent orchestrator; worktree-agent merge branches and AGENTS.md show agents build it.

It's a Halo 2 matching decompilation (C/C++ source) built by Claude/Codex agent lanes (Co-Authored-By trailers, "Codex lane" PRs), but its purpose is the game decomp, not producing software with agents.
The repo is a Kotlin compiler written in Swift (KSwiftK), which is ordinary software. Agent-driven PRs with ticket IDs build it, and it doesn't orchestrate coding agents.
It's a political-life RPG simulation game in TypeScript, and Claude-coauthored commits show agents building it. It isn't a tool for orchestrating coding agents.
xDrive is a file-sync/cloud-drive product (Go server, React web, desktop/mobile clients) with AGENTS.md and agent-style commits, not a tool for orchestrating coding agents.
LoopX is a control plane that orchestrates long-horizon coding agents (Codex, Claude Code) with goals, todos and heartbeats, and its own commits come from the loopx-agent identity.
The repo is an IFC toolkit (WebGPU viewer, parser, Rust geometry kernel) that agents build around the clock, with about 61 merged PRs a day; it is not a tool for orchestrating coding agents.
ThemisDB is a C++ multi-model database, and Copilot agent PRs with "Initial plan" commits are fixing its CI and build, so agents are building a database rather than an agent orchestrator.

README describes dude as a "software factory" whose orchestrator drives implementer, reviewer and fixer agents through to merged pull requests, and the commit history shows it is itself built that way.
README describes a self-hosting autonomous software-delivery system (planning, implementation, review, merge via a workflow graph and GitHub App), and commits show it evolving its own pipeline.

It's a Go CLI toolkit (nova-bus, nova-table, nova-secrets and others) for AI collaboration, not an orchestrator that writes and lands code. Agents (Claude, GPT-6) build it, with many merged PRs a day.
Orgtree is a multi-agent orchestrator with hierarchies, tickets and watchdogs for running AI coding agents, and its commits are co-authored by Claude Opus 5.5.
Leaf is a generative-UI product (a plugin that renders pages and collects comments for Claude Code/Codex), not an orchestrator of coding agents; agents (leaf-agent, "maintained with tend") build it.

The repo is an experimental Kotlin dataflow runtime with demos. Commits carry Claude co-author trailers, and .beads, .claude and AGENTS.md show agents building it, but it doesn't orchestrate agents itself.
Melian is a code review agent (a TypeScript product), not a tool that orchestrates agents to write and land code, and its commits are co-authored by Codex and Claude agents.

The marketplace includes plugins that orchestrate agents to write and land code (implementation:implement-dispatch worker briefs, a pr-pipeline with write lanes and App tokens), and the repo is itself agent-developed.

It is a multi-platform Chinese input method (Rust engine plus native hosts), an ordinary software product, and it is built by agents (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, hundreds of commits a day); it doesn't orchestrate coding agents itself.
Commits add Python verifiers, CI workflows and a Qwen backend wrapper for benchmark qualification. That is a software project built by agents, not a tool for orchestrating coding agents.
It's a competitor-monitoring SaaS (Five to Nine, React Router on Cloudflare Workers) whose commits come from Claude and a worker bot; the product isn't an agent orchestrator.
ObjectStack is a metadata-driven app framework/runtime (specs, CLI, plugins) built by an agent fleet bot; its product isn't an orchestrator that produces software with coding agents.
It is a Python library of schemas, validators and CI drift checks (not an agent orchestrator), and bots and agents keep landing evidence-companion commits in it.

OneUptime is a monitoring/observability platform (product), and its commits carry Claude Opus Co-Authored-By trailers and claude/ branches, so agents build it rather than it orchestrating coding agents.
A SysML v2/KerML runtime, language server and client libraries in Go, with commits mostly by devin-ai-integration[bot]; it's a software product, not an agent orchestrator.
It's a control plane that deploys and manages runtime agents on Kubernetes, not a pipeline for agents to write code, and its AGENTS.md and round-the-clock merges show agents building it.
Orbi is a self-hostable "lights-out software factory" that turns labeled GitHub Issues into reviewed, merged PRs and releases, and its own commits come from orbi-build[bot] (it builds itself).
The repo is the orbi.build marketing website (HTML pages, blog, Cloudflare Worker), built by agents and bots. It is the landing page for the Orbi product, not the orchestrator itself.
OreStudio is a C++/web risk-engine GUI application, and its commits carry Claude co-author trailers and agile story/task IDs, so agents build a regular software product.
The repo is a Rust game server, client and tooling (a game, not an agent orchestrator). Agent governance files and a high volume of merged PRs show agents building it.
README describes an orchestration platform (hub, runners, workflow graphs) for autonomous fleets of coding agents, and commits carry Claude co-author trailers, so agents develop it.
It's a Rust RAW photo editor app; commits have Claude Co-Authored-By trailers and t3code/claude branches, and the MCP server is a feature rather than an agent orchestrator.
It's an agent-factory workflow engine that orchestrates coding agents (Codex, Claude, Cursor) to do work, and its own commits come from codex worktree and Claude sessions.

It's a town platform for agents (mailman, stamp ledger, doorstep generator, map, site, tools/) that agents build and run. It isn't meant to produce software, and much of the repo is letters and ledgers, so "not software" is close.

Evener is a coding agent whose `evener hub` orchestrates many concurrent agent sessions that read, write and run code. Its own history (agent memory, AGENTS.md, ~69 merged PRs/day) shows it is built by agents.
It's a Finnish browser/iOS adventure game (Matkakirja) built with Claude co-authored commits and PRs; it's a game, not an agent-orchestration tool.

The repo is a TypeScript/Three.js singleplayer game demo with a shard engine and SDK, and its agent-written commits (Codex co-author trailers, AGENTS.md) build the game rather than orchestrate agents.

Claudexor is a control plane that orchestrates Claude Code, Codex and Cursor in races with cross-model review, and its own commits come from the ouroboros-agent and carry Claudexor co-author trailers.
It's a fleet manager for parallel Claude Code/Codex sessions, with git worktrees and one-click PRs. Commits are Claude co-authored and have automated review loops.
Loom is an agent orchestrator (Curator/Builder/Judge/Doctor sweeps, loom-daemon), and its own commits are made by Loom agents with Claude co-author trailers and fleet-dispatch bots.
Roundhouse is a Rails-to-multi-target transpiler/compiler (Rust), and commits carry Amp thread IDs and AI co-author trailers, so agents build it; it doesn't orchestrate coding agents.
Fusion is a "software factory" multi-agent orchestrator that plans, builds, reviews and merges code, and its own commits are agent-made tasks (FN-#### with Fusion-Task-Id trailers).
Ruflo is an agent meta-harness/swarm orchestrator for Claude Code and Codex, and its commits are agent-authored (Co-Authored-By RuFlo, "dream" PRs), so it's an agent-built orchestrator.
Farhelm is a fleet manager/supervisor for coding-agent sessions across hosts, and the repo is itself agent-built (plan claims/landings, ~40 merged PRs/day).
TraceDecay is a code-intelligence/MCP tool that helps agents read code but doesn't orchestrate agents to write and land code; agents (Devin, etc.) are building it.
Shipfox is a platform that runs coding agents as CI-like workflows (topics include software-factory), and its repo has agent configs (.claude, .codex, AGENTS.md) and agent-driven commits.
Reusable GitHub Actions pipeline turning issues into PRs via AI agents (clarify, plan, implement, review/autofix, merge train), itself built by codex-bot "AI implementation for issue" commits.
Conductor orchestrates Worker and Reviewer agent sessions that claim roadmap tasks, open PRs and merge them. Agents also develop the repo (claim commits, Claude co-authors, bot-generated status).
Gabbro is a systems programming language with a Rust compiler and Lean proofs, built by Claude/opencode agents, but it is not itself a tool for orchestrating coding agents.

README says Legion runs teams of coding agents (architect, planner, implementer, tester, reviewer, merger) turning issues into PRs, and bot identities such as legion-implementer[bot] author its commits.
The project is a LINE CRM on Cloudflare Workers, a regular app. Commits co-authored by Claude and Codex "train" branches show agents building it, but it isn't an agent orchestrator.
The product is a poker club app (React/Supabase game engine, cashier, tournaments), and an autopilot bot lands agent-written fixes; the repo builds the app rather than orchestrating coding agents.
Smithers is an agentic workflow framework and factory that turns issues into reviewed, landed changes with coding agents, and its commits are authored by codex and Claude co-authors.
It's a legal workspace app (web, API, desktop) with agent config dirs and Claude-generated commits; it isn't a tool for orchestrating coding agents.

README describes storytree as an observability layer beside Claude Code/Codex, a desktop app, CLI and library, not an agent orchestrator; its commits are agent-written increments (Claude co-authored).

TauCeti is a Lean library of formalized mathematics (nearly every commit adds theorems or proofs), which falls under formal proofs or mathematics, not an agent-orchestration tool or an ordinary software project.
README says it runs goals through Codex/Claude CLI workers, gates, and lands changes in main; its commits are worker-written, so it is an agent orchestrator developed by itself.

CRW is a Codex skills and Go runtime for planning, delegating to child agent tasks, verifying and integrating work via Linear and CXC. Its own history shows agent-authored per-issue branches merged into dev.

A Copilot CLI plugin suite for orchestrating agent fleets (worktrees, bridge, dispatch task queues, efforts) with an automated dev-to-main release pipeline, heavy merged-PR throughput, and agent-dispatch loops.
It's a Tauri/Rust personal-AI desktop app and general agent harness, not a pipeline for agents to write and land code. Co-authored-by agent trailers and 549 commits a day show agents build it.
A trucking TMS (accounting, banking, driver PWA) is the product, and agent-written PRs with Cursor/Claude co-authors and lane/OUTBOX protocols are how it's built, not what it does.
It's a Raku interpreter in Rust (a language implementation, not an agent orchestrator), and commits are co-authored by Claude with session links.
Vize is a Rust Vue.js toolchain (compiler, linter, formatter, LSP) developed with agents (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, ~65 commits/day). It is not a tool that orchestrates coding agents.
It's a Rust memory control plane for AI agents, a product rather than an agent-orchestrating pipeline, and its issue-numbered agent-authored PRs show agents building it.
A native macOS dictation and clipboard app in Swift, with agent files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) and about 111 PRs merged per day. It is an end-user product, not an agent orchestrator.
VibeSys is a multi-agent framework (outer-loop designer, implementer, judge agents) that generates systems with coding agents, and its own commits are Claude-session co-authored.
README describes uzi as an AI dark factory that turns issues into reviewed PRs via lead/coder/reviewer agents, and its commits are by uzi-agent and its own skills (uzi-lander, uzi-watcher).
vx is a task runner and build cache for JS monorepos, not an agent-orchestration tool, and its commits carry Claude co-author and session trailers.

README describes a control plane that orchestrates CLI coding agents via workflows/workgroups with merge-back of their Git changes, and the repo is itself agent-developed (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Codex co-author trailers).

Pantopus is a neighborhood platform (backend, web, iOS and Android apps), and its commits are co-authored by Claude and merged as PRs from claude/ and codex/ branches. It builds a product, not an agent tool.

The repo defines web standards (Eleventy site, conformance vectors, custom elements) and is built by agent lanes, drain and review tooling. That tooling supports the project; it isn't the project's purpose.
SharpForge is a C# compiler, runtime and browser IDE in JavaScript; its purpose is not agent orchestration, and its Codex branches and task-ID commits show agents building it.
OrnaDB is a Rust database and language runtime (crates, CLI, LSP). Its high-volume agent-style PR commits build that product, not an agent orchestrator.
